Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
HANDLE OF SKIN GRAFTING BLADE 



( Reaffirmed 1998) 



1- Scope — Covers dimensional and other requirements for handle of skin grafting blade, used in 
plastic surgery. 

2, Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1. 



DIA7-, 



ADJUSTING 
KMOB 




Ail dimensions in millimetres. 
FIG. 1 HANDLE OF SKIN GRAFTING BLADE 

2.1 A deviation of ±2'5 percent shall be allowed on all dimensions except where specified. 
3« Materials 

3.1 Frame — Shall be of stainless steel conforming to Designation 30Cr13, 04Crl8Ni11 or 07Cr18Ni9 
of IS : 1570 ( Part V )-1972 ' Schedulesfor wrought steels: Part V Stainless and heat-resisting steels 
( first revision ) ' or brass having minimum of 70 percent copper. 

3.2 Frame Handle — Shall be of aluminium alloy conforming to 15:617-1959 'Specification for 
aluminium and aluminium alloy ingots and castings for general engineering purposes '. 

4. Manufacture, Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 The frame shall consist of a trunnion in which the fixed jaw is mounted. 

4.2 The movable jaw shall be capable of opening through 45° angle and also to-and-fro movement to 
permit its locking. 

4.3 The trunnion shall be adjustable by knobs fixed on both the ends of the frame to make fine 
adjustment of the biad^ with respect to the guiding rod. 



Adopted 29 February 1976 



@ April 1976, BIS 



Gr1 



BUREAU OF INDIAN STANDARDS

IS: 7980 -1976 

4.4 The handle shall be firm and attached to the frame and shall be independent of the trunnion 
adjustment. 

4.5 The fixed jaw shall have three locking pins equally spaced and the movable jaw which has three 
equally spaced locking holes shall properly fit into them without shake or play. 

4.6 The movable jaw shall be capable of propulsion by means of a fixed lever or any other 
convenient method, 

4.7 The guiding rod shall be absolutely parallel to the central line of the trunnion. 

4.8 The guiding rod shall have freedom of movement along its axis by about 20 mm as well as around 
its own axis. 

4.9 The guiding rod shall have spiral knurling to hold sliced graft and it shall be smooth so as not 
to injure the skin on which it is propelled. 

4.10 In the locked position of the blade and the jaws, the trunnion shall be capable of fine adjust- 
ment by means of adjusting screws fixed on either end of the frame and the adjustments shall give 
a graft of 0'2, 0*4, 06 and 0*8 mm respectively. When the knobs are adjusted from both the sides to 
give the required thickness of skin, the guiding rod and the biade shall be perfectly aligned within 
a deviation of not more than ±0*01 mm. 

4.11 The handle shall be free from burrs, pits, blemishes and other surface defects. 

4.12 The handle, if made from stainless steel, shall be polished bright or dull and passivated. If 
made from brass, it shall be plated chromium over nickel conforming to Service Grade No. 2 of 
IS : 4827-1968 ' Specification for electroplated coatings of nickel and chromium on copper and copper 

alloys '. 

5. Teste 

5.1 Performance — The blades conforming to IS : 3759-1966 ' Specification for blades, skin grafting ' 
shall be fitted in the frame of the handle. The skin shall be grafted by adjusting at various settings 
of the blade. During grafting, the blade shall show no tendency to twist or become loose. The 
parallelism of the blade with the guiding rod shall be tested at various settings by means of feeler 
gauges. 

5.2 Corrosion Resistance — The handle shall show no sign of corrosion when put to boiling and 
autoclaving test as mentioned in IS : 7531-1975 ' Method for boiling and autoclaving test for corrosion 
resistance of stainless steel surgical instruments \ 

6. Marking — Each handle shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's name, 
initials or recognized trade-mark. 

6.1 ISl Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

7. Packing — As agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 



Reprography Unit, BIS, New Delhi, India
